summary: Novo Nordisk A/S (NOVO-B.CO, NASDAQ Copenhagen) is a Danish healthcare company built around its GLP-1 franchise across Diabetes and Obesity care plus a Rare Disease unit; in this Valuatum equity research report dated 30 July 2026 we rate the stock BUY with a 12-month target price of 490.80 DKK against a current price of 329.90 DKK, implying roughly 48.8% upside. Market capitalisation is DKK 1,465.6 bn and enterprise value is DKK 1,485 bn.

The core valuation tension is a heavily growth-oriented enterprise-value allocation under a newly capped U.S. pricing regime. The market assigns 47.4% of the DKK 1,485,021 million enterprise value (DKK 703,431m) to Obesity care, which generated only 28.4% of FY2025 segment revenue, and a further 15.8% (DKK 234,477m) to a pre-revenue growth pipeline dented by CagriSema's REDEFINE 4 miss, while the mature Diabetes care profit engine delivers 71.6% of segment sales yet carries just 36.8% of EV. FY25 net sales of DKK 309,064m are guided down to ~DKK 293,810m in FY26 (-4.9%) under the $350/month Medicare price cap, yet EBITDA is forecast to rise to DKK 151,392m (+4.3%) as the DKK 8bn restructuring program offsets pricing compression.

On a reverse-valuation basis the debate is whether Medicare-driven volume can outrun the price caps: obesity patient volume must scale from 2.8m toward roughly 4.0m to rebuild EBIT under capped pricing. The base case applies a 16.0x EV/EBITDA multiple to 2027E EBITDA of DKK 142,633m, implying DKK 490.18 per share (+48.6%) and anchoring the BUY call; the bull case of oral Wegovy unlocking 6+ million patients implies DKK 426.68 (+29.3%), while the bear case of Zepbound capturing over 60% of the incremental Medicare market compresses the multiple to 7.8x and implies DKK 178.39 (-45.9%).

thesis.title: Obesity volume scales to defend EBIT
thesis.text: Obesity patient volume must scale from 2.8m to roughly 4.0m under the $350/month Medicare price cap to generate DKK 116,250m in segment revenue at a 40% margin, protecting the DKK 46,500m EBIT that justifies obesity care's 15x multiple and 45% EV allocation.

thesis.title: Cost cuts offset pricing compression
thesis.text: FY26 EBITDA is guided up 4.3% to DKK 151,392m despite a 4.9% sales decline, as the DKK 8bn restructuring program offsets pricing compression, supporting the 16.0x EV/EBITDA multiple used to anchor the DKK 490.8 target price.

thesis.title: Pipeline optionality faces clinical risk
thesis.text: The growth pipeline accounts for 15% of EV (DKK 232,437m) and needs DKK 77,500m in peak sales to justify that value. This looks doubtful after CagriSema's REDEFINE 4 miss (23.0% weight loss versus Zepbound's 25.5%), leaving valuation risk unresolved pending 2026-2027 catalysts.

thesisBreaker: If Eli Lilly's Zepbound captures >60% of the incremental Medicare volume due to superior efficacy, Novo's massive fixed costs will permanently compress margins and drag equity value below DKK 800 billion.

valuePools.name: Obesity care
valuePools.economics: Revenue DKK 82,347m (28.4%) · Comp. EBIT DKK 33,957m (28.4% of EBIT) · EV DKK 703,431m
valuePools.text: Scaling pool priced as the primary growth engine of the enterprise, pivoting from a high-margin, supply-constrained therapeutic to a mass-market, high-volume franchise after Most-Favored-Nation pricing and the TrumpRx program capped Wegovy at $350 per month ($150 for oral formulations). The valuation now rests on the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program offering $50 copays to millions of beneficiaries from July 2026, in a U.S. market where the obesity rate stands near 40% and Medicare coverage expands the addressable pool by an estimated 10 to 40 million individuals. Eli Lilly holds the efficacy lead after REDEFINE 4 (Zepbound 25.5% weight loss versus CagriSema 23.0% at 84 weeks), so Novo leans on the newly launched oral Wegovy pill, DKK 84bn of Catalent capex and the DKK 8-9 billion restructuring charge targeting DKK 8 billion in annual savings by the end of 2026; segment growth in FY25 was 31% CER.

valuePools.name: Growth pipeline / optionality
valuePools.economics: Revenue DKK 0m (0.0%) · Comp. EBIT DKK 0m (0.0% of EBIT) · EV DKK 234,477m
valuePools.text: Emerging option covering next-generation obesity (CagriSema) and the Akero MASH asset efruxifermin, which is pending regulatory approval. The allocation was priced as an inevitable succession plan until the REDEFINE 4 Phase 3 trial failed its primary non-inferiority endpoint against Zepbound (23.0% vs 25.5% weight loss at 84 weeks), forcing a retreat to a higher-dose 2.4/7.2 mg formulation in the REDEFINE 11 trial and pushing potential commercialization of a superior agent to 2027 or beyond. At a mature 3x peak-sales multiple, justifying the DKK 232 billion EV allocation requires a credible path to roughly DKK 77 billion in un-risked annual sales.

valuePools.name: Diabetes care
valuePools.economics: Revenue DKK 207,109m (71.6%) · Comp. EBIT DKK 85,693m (71.6% of EBIT) · EV DKK 547,113m
valuePools.text: Profit engine and the core of current cash generation, priced as an annuity nearing its terminal growth phase with a conscious maturity discount. The GLP-1 diabetes franchise (Ozempic, Rybelsus) and the legacy insulin business generate the strong free cash flow needed to fund the DKK 84 billion in gross capex scaling the Obesity franchise. The compressed multiple reflects two headwinds: the U.S. pricing interventions cap Ozempic at $350 per month, and semaglutide faces loss of exclusivity in select international markets starting in 2026. The valuation depends not on growth but on the DKK 8 billion restructuring program defending operating margins as the top line softens.

reverseValuation.intro: The scenario bridge tests whether the revenue, margin and multiple assumptions embedded in Novo Nordisk's enterprise value are coherent, with the Obesity care volume ramp following Medicare access and the competitive balance with Eli Lilly as the swing factors. The bull case requires the oral Wegovy pill capturing low-cost patients and unlocking 6+ million patients, while the bear case involves Zepbound capturing over 60% of the incremental Medicare market on clinical superiority; enterprise value bridges to equity via the deduction of DKK 104,494 million in net debt.

coreAnalysis.heading: How the company creates economic value
coreAnalysis.text: Novo Nordisk generates nearly all of its economic output from its core GLP-1 franchise spanning the mature Diabetes care business and the rapidly scaling Obesity care business; in FY2025 the combined Diabetes and Obesity care segment accounted for 93.7% of group net sales (DKK 289,456 million) and a commensurate share of the DKK 127,658 million reported group EBIT. The enterprise-value allocation diverges materially from the revenue mix: the market assigns 45% of the DKK 1,549,580 million group enterprise value to Obesity care despite it generating only ~27% of current sales, while the cash-generative Diabetes base (67% of sales) carries just 35% of enterprise value, a further 15% sits in future pipeline optionality and only 5% in the stable but small Rare Disease unit. This EV bridges to the DKK 1,445,086 million equity market capitalization via the deduction of DKK 104,494 million in net debt, a balance inflated by the DKK 83,993 million gross capex spike tied to the Catalent manufacturing acquisitions. Management has guided to a 5-13% decline in adjusted net sales and EBIT at constant exchange rates for FY2026, driven by major structural U.S. pricing changes.

coreAnalysis.heading: Cross-pool bridge
coreAnalysis.text: The near-term forecast is driven mechanically by the clash between surging patient volumes and structurally lower unit pricing: the FY26 guidance of a ~5% top-line decline comes almost entirely from Diabetes and Obesity care absorbing U.S. MFN pricing and the TrumpRx implementation. While revenue contracts, EBITDA is forecast to hold or slightly expand, engineered directly by the Q3 2025 restructuring program that eliminated 9,000 positions to extract DKK 8 billion in annual savings. The bridge from EBITDA to EBIT exposes the capital intensity of the new model, with depreciation and amortization forecast to nearly double from DKK 17.4 billion to over DKK 30 billion in 2026 on the DKK 84 billion Catalent acquisitions. Approximately 85% of the DKK 1,549,580 million enterprise value is supported by the current commercial earnings engine, and with the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program opening access at a $50 copay, the volume necessary to generate DKK ~100 billion in combined segment EBIT is entirely realistic; the fragile portion is the 15% of EV (DKK 232 billion) allocated to a pipeline badly damaged by CagriSema's failure to prove superiority over Zepbound.

coreAnalysis.heading: Scenarios and verdict
coreAnalysis.text: The scenarios diverge on the execution of the Obesity care volume ramp and the competitive balance with Eli Lilly. In the bull case, the $150/month oral Wegovy pill captures patients unwilling to take injections and Catalent capacity allows Novo to supply 6+ million patients, with the resulting EBITDA expansion supporting a DKK 2 trillion enterprise value. The bear case materializes if the clinical superiority of Lilly's tirzepatide dictates market share in the newly expanded Medicare population: the pipeline optionality is written down to zero, the core franchise multiple compresses to 10x EV/EBIT, and equity value is dragged below DKK 800 billion, with DKK 104 billion of net debt amplifying the downside. The central mid-2026 debate is whether Novo can navigate the transition from a high-price, low-volume biologics innovator to a lower-margin, mass-market manufacturing giant; the DKK 1.55 trillion enterprise value is predominantly supported by current economics, provided the newly uncapped U.S. Medicare volume can mathematically overpower the strict $350/month price ceilings imposed by the 2025 regulatory interventions.

risks: Structural pricing risk (Obesity care): commercial payers use the $350 government benchmark to force even lower net prices, with declining private-market gross margins as the early warning - HIGH impact and a thesis-breaker if it occurs.

Clinical inferiority risk (Growth pipeline / optionality): higher-dose trials (REDEFINE 11) fail due to gastrointestinal side effects, with elevated patient dropout rates in trials as the early warning - HIGH impact, structural.

Manufacturing execution risk (Obesity care): integration stalls or FDA compliance issues arise at the acquired Catalent sites, with failure to hit the DKK 8bn savings run-rate as the early warning - MEDIUM impact, manageable.
catalysts: U.S. Medicare GLP-1 Bridge uptake (near-term, Obesity care): quarterly Wegovy prescription volumes versus Zepbound dictate Obesity volume growth; prescription uptake in the second half of 2026 after the July implementation is the most critical catalyst for the thesis.

CagriSema FDA decision (medium-term, Growth pipeline / optionality): label restrictions and head-to-head efficacy language validate the pipeline regulatory path; given the REDEFINE 4 miss, how the label compares to Zepbound matters more than the approval itself.
Akero efruxifermin (MASH) approval (medium-term, Growth pipeline / optionality): FDA approval triggering the $0.5bn CVR derisks the MASH optionality embedded in the enterprise value.
CagriSema higher-dose REDEFINE 11 data (long-term, Growth pipeline / optionality): weight loss above 25% with acceptable GI tolerability rebuilds or destroys the pipeline EV.

faqs.q: Is Novo Nordisk a buy in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Valuatum's 30 July 2026 equity report rates Novo Nordisk (NOVO-B.CO) a BUY with a 490.80 DKK 12-month target versus a 329.90 DKK price, implying about 48.8% upside. The re-rating hinges on whether Medicare-driven volume can outrun the $350/month U.S. price cap fast enough to defend absolute EBIT.

faqs.q: What is Novo Nordisk's price target?
faqs.a: The Valuatum report dated 30 July 2026 sets a 12-month fundamental target price of 490.80 DKK for Novo Nordisk (NOVO-B.CO), against a current price of 329.90 DKK. The target is anchored by a 16.0x EV/EBITDA multiple on 2027E EBITDA of DKK 142,633m, versus a 21.5x normalized historical average and Eli Lilly at 41.0x.

faqs.q: Why is Novo Nordisk rated BUY?
faqs.a: Novo Nordisk is rated BUY because the stock trades at just 14.2x 2026E earnings and 9.8x EV/EBITDA while the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program opens access to tens of millions of new patients at a $50 copay from July 2026. FY26 EBITDA is guided up 4.3% to DKK 151,392m despite a 4.9% sales decline, as the DKK 8bn restructuring program offsets the new pricing caps.

On Valuatum's framework Novo Nordisk looks undervalued: the 16.0x 2027E EV/EBITDA used in the valuation is a discount to the company's 21.5x historical normalized average and to Eli Lilly's 41.0x. The ROE-versus-P/BV cross-check points the same way, as a forecast average ROE of 38.4% implies a 5.7x P/BV and a DKK 377.8 share price, about 15% above the current DKK 329.9 quote.

faqs.q: How does the reverse valuation work for Novo Nordisk?
faqs.a: The scenario bridge tests the assumptions behind the enterprise value, with the Obesity volume ramp and competition from Eli Lilly as the swing factors. The base case applies 16.0x to DKK 142,633m of 2027E EBITDA, implying DKK 490.18 per share (+48.6%). The bull case of oral Wegovy unlocking 6+ million patients implies DKK 426.68, while the bear case of Zepbound taking over 60% of the incremental Medicare volume compresses the multiple to 7.8x and implies DKK 178.39.
